title: The Real Danger of Big Tech
gist: Howard French argues the more imminent AI danger is the concentration of political power in a few tech billionaires, led by Musk, who are shaping US government, retirement policy and tax fights, creating risk of state capture.

insights.claim: The US government now depends on Musk, a trillionaire since June, for its space program, global communications and competitiveness in electric vehicles and batteries.
insights.speaker: Howard W. French
insights.so_what: Single-person dependence adds governance and key-man risk for government-linked contracts.

insights.claim: The WSJ reported Musk ordered a slowdown of Starlink's military-grade service for Ukraine, while Reuters reported the decision came from the White House; Trump denies involvement.
insights.speaker: Howard W. French
insights.so_what: Unclear chain of command over critical infrastructure is a risk for allies.
insights.locator: A parallel and equally shocking example

insights.claim: Musk gave an unusually direct warning to Congress members considering investigating him, and is described as the largest campaign financier in US politics with hundreds of millions to Republicans.
insights.speaker: Howard W. French
insights.so_what: If Democrats win the House, expect oversight conflict involving Musk firms.
insights.quote: Those who pick fights with me should understand that I will find out who is really pulling the strings and come for them
insights.locator: Musk, though, who has been the least inhibited

insights.claim: Musk’s pledge of one SpaceX share to every US child, worth as much as $11 billion, is read as tax-saving and a bid for a position in the looming Social Security debate through creeping privatization.
insights.speaker: Howard W. French
insights.so_what: Watch billionaire child-account schemes as an entry into retirement and financial services.

insights.claim: Zuckerberg arranged a new nonvoting share class to pay any California wealth-tax bill without diluting control, while AI-industry leaders back a campaign against Proposition 40, on the November ballot.
insights.speaker: Howard W. French
insights.so_what: Proposition 40 is a catalyst for California tax risk on AI-linked wealth.

insights.claim: Bezos has reshaped the Washington Post toward pro-business editorials, which French links to his interest in currying favor with the White House.
insights.speaker: Howard W. French
insights.so_what: Media ownership by firms with government exposure carries bias risk.
insights.locator: Jeff Bezos, the founder of Amazon

insights.claim: French says a consensus is forming that concentrated AI-era fortunes are shifting US politics toward state capture, where private interests predominate over public ones.
insights.speaker: Howard W. French
insights.so_what: Frames AI wealth as a political-risk factor for regulation of the sector.

insights.claim: Musk has advocated limiting nonwhite migration to the West and pushed Trump to ease entry for white South Africans.
insights.speaker: Howard W. French
